$comment: THE CLASSIFICATION IS DATA, NOT CODE. Which paths count as shipped value is a PROJECT question, not a kernel one (Tiphys DR-0029: the kernel owns orchestration, the project supplies its own definition of done). So value-ratio.mjs ships the mechanism and every project ships one of these. RULES ARE ORDERED AND FIRST MATCH WINS, which is why the order below is load-bearing rather than tidy: the named root files come first so that a later broad `*.md` rule cannot swallow AGENTS.md, assurance comes before value so that a test living inside a value tree stays assurance, and paperwork comes before the value directories so that a subject project's own delivery/ folder is not counted as the thing it delivers. The default bucket is deliberately `overhead` rather than `value`, because an unclassified path is one nobody claimed, and counting it as value is the flattering error.

buckets.value: Changes to paths the consumer of this project actually receives. For a library or CLI that is the shipped source and the declared package contents.
buckets.assurance: Changes whose purpose is to prove the value paths work: tests, witnesses, gate scripts, CI configuration, measurement tools. Not waste, and deliberately NOT gated, because gating it makes reviewing less the cheapest way to pass.
buckets.overhead: Everything else. Process paperwork, plans, reviews, evidence, decision records, agent rules. This is the bucket the budget constrains.

rules.$comment: Named root files that ship, listed first so the paperwork rule's `*.md` cannot claim AGENTS.md.
Proof that the value paths work. Before the value rules so a test inside a value tree stays assurance.
Process paperwork at any depth. Before the value rules so a subject project's own delivery/ is not counted as delivered value.
